user_input: I can't even open my IDE without seeing her name in our old shared git repos. We broke up three weeks ago, right before the midterms, and now I'm sitting in this empty double-occupancy hostel room alone because my roommate went home for the weekend. I flunked my Amazon OA today because my head was spinning with our old late-night coding chats, and she’s already posting pictures smiling with her new project group. I feel so incredibly discarded, like I'm just a bug in her code she patched out while I'm drowning in backlogs.

Everyone in my wing is out celebrating their placement offers, and I'm just staring at my fan in this dark hostel room. He was the only one who didn't care about my CGPA or how many questions I solved on LeetCode; he just listened when my anxiety spiked. Now that we're over, the silence in this room is deafening, and I have no one to tell that my dad compared my package to my cousin's again today. I feel like my safety net has been ripped away and I'm just free-falling into nothing.

I had to skip dinner today because I saw her sitting at our usual table in the mess hall, laughing with some guy from the robotics club. We spent two years together, sharing lunch boxes and studying for end-sems, and now I have to sneak around my own hostel like a criminal just to avoid seeing her move on. I ended up buying a packet of raw Maggi from the tuck shop and eating it dry in my room, feeling like a total loser. How did I go from being her whole world to someone who can't even eat in public anymore?

I found myself scrolling through our WhatsApp media folder from last semester, back when we’d study in the library till 2 AM and then walk back to the girls' hostel under the streetlights. Tomorrow is what would have been our two-year anniversary, and instead of celebrating, I'm trying to debug an OS assignment that's due at midnight. My lab partners are all talking about their weekend trips in the group chat, and I've never felt more invisible or disconnected from my peers. It feels like everyone’s life is moving forward in high-speed while I’m stuck looping on the same painful memory.

I saw my ex’s Instagram story of her hanging out with our old mutual friends at the campus cafe, the exact same spot where we used to sit after our coding labs. Since we broke up, none of those guys have texted me once, and I realize they were only my friends because of her. I’m sitting here with a cold cup of tea, listening to the rain hit my hostel window, feeling utterly discarded by both love and friendship. I feel like an NPC in everyone else's life, totally disposable and easily forgotten once the main character leaves.

We broke up last week, right before the TCS day-1 placements started. She already got placed in a Tier-1 firm and I'm sitting here in my empty room with a 6.8 CGPA, staring at our old WhatsApp chats and wondering how someone can just delete three years of their life so easily. Everyone else is celebrating their offers in the hostel mess, and I can't even swallow my food without feeling like I'm going to throw up from the quiet.

I used to finish my DSA labs at 10 PM and immediately call him to vent about how toxic our professor is. Now, I walk back to my room in the dark and my phone doesn't vibrate once. The silence in this hostel corridor is physical; it actually hurts my chest, and I find myself just sitting on the floor staring at the wall because going inside my room means accepting that nobody is waiting to hear how my day went anymore.

Today was supposed to be our two-year anniversary, and instead of the dinner we planned, I'm hiding in the library pretending to study for the SQL midterms. I saw her walking past the Nescafe stall with someone else from the CSE department, laughing at some joke, and it felt like a physical punch to the stomach. How is she moving on so fast while I'm still stuck trying to survive backlogs and this crushing, hollow feeling in my chest?

My ex and I shared the same friend group in college, but since the breakup, they all went out for a trip to the hills this weekend and nobody even asked me if I wanted to come. I spent the entire Saturday evening scrolling through their Instagram stories in my dark hostel room, eating cold Maggie. It's like I didn't just lose my partner, I lost my entire social safety net, and now I'm just this invisible ghost haunting the campus.

We broke up over a text during the end-semester break, and now that we're back on campus, the silence is killing me. I can't listen to my Spotify playlist anymore because every single song we shared just brings back the memory of us studying together in the library. I have an operating systems exam tomorrow, but I've just been staring at the ceiling for six hours because the sheer loneliness of this room feels like it's crushing my ribcage.

Everyone in my wing is grinding LeetCode or celebrating their Day 1 placements, and I’m just staring at my VS Code terminal with tears blurring the screen. My ex and I used to pull all-nighters together in the library, and now my Spotify 'Friends Activity' shows them listening to our favorite lofi playlist with someone else. I can't focus on my trees or graphs when my phone is so dead, and my room feels like an absolute tomb.

I sat through a three-hour DSA lab today pretending to debug code, but I was just looking at our old chat exports on my drive. Everyone else has a group or a partner to share the load, but I'm just this broken, failing burden that nobody wants to stay with.

I ended up scrolling through my ex's Instagram and saw them posting pictures at a cafe we used to go to, looking completely fine. My stomach is in knots because I haven’t eaten all day, and the thought of going down to the mess hall alone and seeing all the couples laughing together makes me want to throw up.

It's 2 AM and I’ve been staring at our old Spotify playlist for two hours instead of studying for tomorrow's System Design quiz. I feel so pathetic for being this broken over someone who isn't even looking back.

I'm sitting here with a 6.2 CGPA, no placement offers, and absolutely no one to talk to because I cut off my other friends to spend all my time with her. It’s raining outside and the entire hostel wing is empty because everyone went home for the long weekend, except me because I couldn't afford the train ticket. I've become a ghost in my own life, just drifting from one boring lecture to another without any anchor.

Every shared song that plays just makes me feel like a complete loser who ruined the best thing he ever had.

If it was this easy for him to forget me, did our relationship even mean anything at all?

Today would have been our three-year anniversary. My room is completely silent and the loneliness is so loud it's making me dizzy. I tried coding to distract myself but I just ended up staring at the blank IDE for hours.

I can't sleep. It's 3 AM and the hostel is completely quiet except for the rain outside. I feel like such an idiot for still missing someone who chose to walk away while I'm left drowning in academic pressure and isolation.

She was my entire support system here, and now that she’s gone, I realize I have zero actual friends in this college. Now I'm totally alone, drowning in my syllabus, and carrying this massive guilt that I ruined the only good thing in my life.

I feel like a complete burden to everyone around me, so I just lock my door and stay in bed all day, disappearing more and more.

I can't even study for the upcoming Capgemini drive because the silence in this room is literally choking me.

I tried opening my DBMS slides tonight but I just stared at the screen crying because we used to group-study this exact unit in the library basement.

The thought of being in that crowded auditorium surrounded by thousands of happy people makes me feel so unbelievably, pathetically alone.

We broke up right before the midterms, and now I can't even open my DSA assignment without seeing our shared Google Docs history. Everyone in the hostel is grinding for placements, talking about 20 LPA packages, while I'm just staring at my blank IDE crying. We used to study together in the library until 2 AM, and now walking past those tables makes my chest physically ache. I feel completely hollow and left behind by everyone.

She blocked me on everything last night.
